attempts.summary: Implemented via Ansible (executed from node4, the pre-configured control node) a WireGuard gateway topology: node2 serves an app on TCP/8080 bound only to a private-link IP (10.10.20.2) shared with node1 over a dedicated NIC; node3 (outside that private network) reaches the app exclusively through a WireGuard tunnel (10.200.0.0/24) terminated on node1 (VyOS), with VyOS firewall/NAT restricting forwarded traffic to wg0->10.10.20.2:8080 only, and node2's app not bound to any public interface. Ansible project lives on node4 at /root/ansible (site.yml + roles gateway/app/client) with inventory at /root/inventory.ini; verified idempotent via two full re-runs and an in-playbook verification play asserting tunnel access works and the direct public-IP path is blocked. Completed the mandatory per-node restart protocol on all four nodes, confirming changed boot IDs and full post-restart recovery of connectivity/services, including end-to-end app access through the tunnel after node1's reboot.
